Method and scope

How this was done

What was examined

Full crawl of the www property across the US, CA and UK storefronts. Covers indexation, crawl efficiency, structured data, internationalisation, page experience and internal linking. Excludes the help centre subdomain, the careers site and paid landing pages under /lp/, which are noindexed by design and out of contract for this engagement.

What it was built from
SourceWindowConfidence
Screaming Frog SEO Spider 21.4 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-13 High
Google Search Console, Pages and Performance reports 2026-05-15 to 2026-08-12 High
Server access logs, Cloudflare Logpush 2026-07-14 to 2026-08-13 High
PageSpeed Insights field data, CrUX 28 day rolling to 2026-08-12 Medium
Ahrefs Site Explorer 2026-08-12 snapshot Medium
Manual review, Chrome 141 and Googlebot smartphone UA 2026-08-13 to 2026-08-18 High
What it could not see

Log coverage starts 14 July, so anything before that is inferred from Search Console rather than observed at the server. The Shopify checkout flow could not be crawled with an authenticated session, so cart and checkout templates were reviewed manually on three sample journeys rather than at scale. CrUX field data is unavailable for the CA storefront because it sits below the reporting threshold, so mobile page experience for Canada is estimated from lab data only. No access to the CMS staging environment was granted, so effort estimates for template level fixes are the consultant's judgement rather than a developer's.

How priority is worked out

Every finding is scored the same way, so the ordering is arithmetic rather than opinion. Effort sits under a square root deliberately: dividing by it outright would make the register recommend nothing but trivia.

score = 3 × (severity × reach × confidence × leverage) ÷ sqrt(effort) × risk factor, capped at 100

The band is a position inside this audit rather than a fixed number: P1 is the most urgent work here, not a score above some threshold. Two findings that score the same always share a band.

P2Next 25%Scheduled work
P3Next 30%Do alongside

P1 Crawling/Waste/1 Found August 14, 2026

Faceted navigation exposes 41,286 crawlable parameter URLs that duplicate 214 category pages

Priority
P195 of 100
Do this first
Effort

Owner

Where
Category listing template, Collection filter template
URLs affected
41,286

Crawl waste
Who feels it

When it bites

Confidence
High
Markets
US, CA, UK
Client decision
Accepted
Why it matters

Measured from 30 days of Cloudflare Logpush records filtered to verified Googlebot by reverse DNS. 1,412,880 Googlebot requests total, 542,545 of which resolved to URLs carrying a filter parameter.

The evidence, gathered July 14, 2026 to August 13, 2026
Unique URLs returning 200 under /collections/ with one or more filter parameters41,286 Screaming Frog › Crawl
Distinct rendered title tags across those URLs214 Screaming Frog › Crawl
Googlebot requests to filtered URLs as a share of all crawl requests, 30 day log window38.4 percent Server logs › Bot requests
Filtered URLs carrying a self referencing canonical41,286 of 41,286 Screaming Frog › Crawl

Confidence is high. Three independent sources agree. The crawler enumerated the URL space directly, the server logs confirm Googlebot is fetching them at scale, and Search Console reports 36,900 URLs in Discovered, currently not indexed. Nothing here rests on estimation.

2 Exhibits
The fix

Stop the filtered URL space from being crawled at all, rather than trying to consolidate it after the fact. Canonicals are already correct and Google is ignoring them because the volume is too high for the crawler to reconcile.

  1. 1Add a robots.txt disallow for /collections/*?*filter= and the four other filter parameter prefixes found in the crawl
  2. 2Strip filter parameters from every internal link in the facet component so no crawlable path into the space remains, with SEO reviewing the change before it ships
  3. 3Return the parameter URLs as noindex,follow for 60 days before the disallow lands, so already indexed variants can drop out
  4. 4Set the Shopify theme to render facet state client side after the first interaction rather than as a link href
  5. 5Re-pull the log sample 30 days after deploy and confirm the filtered share of crawl is below 5 percent

Waiting on Fortnightly theme deploy window

How we will know it worked

Re-run the Screaming Frog crawl with the same configuration and confirm fewer than 500 filtered URLs return 200. Pull 30 days of logs and confirm filtered URLs are under 5 percent of verified Googlebot requests. Check the Search Console Pages report for a fall in Discovered, currently not indexed.

Check again by October 15, 2026.

What has happened since

Accepted by the client. Approved for the October theme release.

Why it matters

Count of distinct product URLs whose only internal link path runs through a paginated category page at ?page=2 or deeper, taken from the Screaming Frog inlink report. Verified by removing category paths from the link graph and re-running the orphan report.

The evidence, gathered August 11, 2026 to August 13, 2026
Category pages at ?page=2 or higher carrying a canonical to the unparameterised URL1,206 of 1,206 Screaming Frog › Crawl
Products reachable only from page two or deeper8,940 Screaming Frog › Crawl
Those products present in the Search Console index1,317 of 8,940 Search Console › URL Inspection

Confidence is high. The canonical behaviour was read directly from rendered HTML on all 1,206 pages. The index coverage figure comes from the URL Inspection API run against a random sample of 400 of the 8,940 orphaned products, extrapolated with a stated margin, so the product count is measured and the index count is a sample estimate.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Make each paginated page self canonical so the products it links to stay in the crawl graph, and give the deep tail a second discovery path that does not depend on pagination at all.

  1. 1Change the canonical on ?page=2 and deeper to reference the paginated URL itself
  2. 2Keep the noindex off those pages, they should be indexable and thin, not absent
  3. 3Publish an HTML sitemap of every product grouped by category, linked from the footer
  4. 4Confirm the XML sitemap lists all 4,213 products, it currently lists 3,006
  5. 5Request validation in the Search Console Pages report once deployed
How we will know it worked

Crawl the category templates and confirm every paginated URL is self canonical. Re-run the orphan report and confirm zero products are reachable only through pagination. Track impressions for the affected product set in Search Console over the following six weeks.

Check again by October 1, 2026.

What has happened since

Accepted by the client. Approved. Platform engineering has started on the pagination template.

Direct count from parsing the JSON-LD block on all 4,213 crawled product pages and testing each against the Product schema requirements Google publishes for merchant listings.

The evidence, gathered August 11, 2026 to August 15, 2026

Those blocks passing the Rich Results Test without error200 of 4,213 Rich Results Test › Live test

Confidence is high. Every product page was crawled and its JSON-LD extracted and parsed, so this is a census rather than a sample. Search Console independently reports 4,011 items with issues against my 4,013, a two page difference explained by pages published after the crawl.

2 Exhibits
The fix

Fix the two missing properties in the Shopify product schema template. Both values are already available in Liquid, neither needs new data.

  1. 1Add offers.priceValidUntil rendering as the current date plus 365 days
  2. 2Add aggregateRating.reviewCount from the review app metafield, and suppress the whole aggregateRating node when reviewCount is zero rather than emitting an empty rating
  3. 3Validate 20 sample pages across all six markets in the Rich Results Test before deploy
  4. 4Request validation in the Search Console Merchant listings report after deploy

Waiting on Review app metafield mapping needs confirming with the merchandising team

How we will know it worked

Re-crawl all product pages with the same custom extraction and confirm zero blocks are missing either property. Confirm the Search Console Merchant listings report moves the affected items to Valid. Spot check five pages in the Rich Results Test per market.

Check again by September 30, 2026.

What has happened since

Accepted by the client. Approved. Small enough to go out with the next front end release.

Count of verified Googlebot requests with a path beginning /search in 30 days of Cloudflare Logpush records, reverse DNS verified.

The evidence, gathered July 14, 2026 to August 13, 2026
URLs under /search?q= returning 200 and indexable12,407 Screaming Frog › Crawl
Those URLs present in the Google index by site: sampleapproximately 900 Manual review › Search results
Googlebot requests to /search in the 30 day log window81,340 Server logs › Bot requests

Confidence is high. The crawl enumerated the URLs and the logs confirm Googlebot is fetching them. The index count is a site: operator sample rather than a Search Console figure, so it is directionally right rather than exact, and I have said so rather than quoting it as measured.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Block internal search from robots.txt and remove the internal links that feed it.

  1. 1Add Disallow: /search to robots.txt
  2. 2Add noindex to the search template for 30 days before the disallow, so indexed results drop out first
  3. 3Remove the popular searches module from the footer, which is the only internal link source into the space
How we will know it worked

Fetch robots.txt and confirm the disallow is live. Re-run the crawl and confirm /search URLs are no longer reachable from an internal link. Confirm Googlebot requests to /search fall below 1,000 per 30 days in the logs.

Check again by September 20, 2026.

What has happened since

Accepted by the client. Approved on the interim readout call so it could ship with the August theme release.

Reported live on August 27, 2026.

Deployed with the 27 August theme release. Logs for the following week show Googlebot requests to /search down from roughly 2,700 per day to 46. Leaving open for a further 30 days to confirm the indexed results drop out before marking verified.

Count taken from the Screaming Frog hreflang report, which resolves each declared alternate and checks for a reciprocal declaration. Manually verified on twelve sampled pages by fetching both sides of the pair.

The evidence, gathered August 11, 2026 to August 16, 2026
Pages emitting an hreflang cluster3,908 Screaming Frog › Hreflang
Clusters where en-CA is referenced but does not reference back1,402 Screaming Frog › Hreflang
Search Console International Targeting errors reportedno data, report retired Search Console › Legacy reports

Confidence is medium. The missing return tags are measured directly from the crawl and are not in doubt. What is uncertain is the consequence. Google states unreciprocated annotations may be ignored, but the CA storefront sits below the CrUX reporting threshold and Search Console does not break performance out by hreflang cluster, so I cannot show the traffic effect, only the defect.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Make the hreflang block render from a single shared market map rather than per template, so reciprocity cannot drift again.

  1. 1Move the hreflang block out of the three templates and into one shared snippet driven by the market map
  2. 2Include x-default pointing at the US storefront
  3. 3Re-crawl and confirm every declared alternate reciprocates
  4. 4Add an hreflang reciprocity check to the monthly crawl so a regression is caught rather than found in the next audit

Waiting on Market map needs sign off from the localisation lead

How we will know it worked

Re-run the Screaming Frog hreflang report and confirm zero unreciprocated annotations across all six markets. Fetch three pairs per market by hand and confirm both sides declare each other.

Check again by November 1, 2026.

What has happened since

Deferred by the client. Parked until the localisation lead signs off the market map.

Why it matters

CrUX 28 day rolling field data for the origin, filtered to the /collections/ URL group and mobile form factor, pulled 12 August. Only 31 percent of visits meet the good threshold of 2.5 seconds.

The evidence, gathered July 16, 2026 to August 17, 2026
CrUX 75th percentile LCP, mobile, /collections/ URL group4.8 seconds PageSpeed Insights › Field (CrUX)
Share of mobile visits meeting the good LCP threshold31 percent PageSpeed Insights › Field (CrUX)
LCP element identified in labhero banner img, unsized, lazy loaded Chrome DevTools › Performance trace
Hero image transfer size, mobile viewport612 KB served at 2400px wide Chrome DevTools › Network

Confidence is medium. The field data is real user data and reliable for the US and UK groups. The cause is a lab observation from six traced page loads on a throttled connection, so the diagnosis is well supported but not proven at scale. Canada is excluded from the claim entirely because CrUX has no data for that storefront.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Give the hero image explicit dimensions, stop lazy loading it, and serve a viewport appropriate source. The element is above the fold on every category page and is the LCP candidate in every trace.

  1. 1Remove loading=lazy from the hero image, it is always above the fold
  2. 2Add width and height attributes so the layout does not shift while it loads
  3. 3Add a srcset with 640, 960 and 1440 wide sources and a sizes attribute matching the template
  4. 4Add fetchpriority=high to the hero img
  5. 5Re-measure in the lab, then wait 28 days for the field data to move

Waiting on Design needs to supply the 640 and 960 wide crops

How we will know it worked

Re-run PageSpeed Insights on ten category URLs and confirm the lab LCP is under 2.5 seconds. Wait a full 28 day CrUX window after deploy and confirm the field 75th percentile is under 2.5 seconds and the good share is above 75 percent.

Check again by November 15, 2026.

Screaming Frog near duplicate analysis at a 95 percent similarity threshold, confirmed by diffing the extracted intro block across all 214 category pages.

The evidence, gathered August 11, 2026 to August 18, 2026

Confidence is medium. The duplication is measured and certain. Whether it matters is a judgement. These pages still rank and the duplication is internal rather than cross domain, so I have weighted this as a quality problem to fix opportunistically rather than a ranking emergency, and I would not claim a traffic figure for it.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Replace the shared block with a short intro written per category. This is a content task, not an engineering one, and it can run in the background across a quarter.

  1. 1Write a 60 to 90 word intro per category, prioritising the 30 categories that carry the most organic entrances
  2. 2Remove the shared block entirely rather than leaving it below the new copy
  3. 3Leave the remaining categories without an intro rather than filling them with the shared block

Waiting on Category priority list from the analytics team

How we will know it worked

Re-run the near duplicate report and confirm no two category pages exceed 80 percent similarity on the intro block. Spot check the top 30 categories by hand.

Check again by January 15, 2027.

What has happened since

Rejected by the client. The shared introduction is a brand requirement from merchandising. Not changing it this year.

Observed by loading twelve pages across the DE and FR storefronts in a clean Chrome 141 profile with no stored consent, and measuring rendered main element content before and after interacting with the banner.

The evidence, gathered August 19, 2026
Rendered main content bytes before consent, DE storefront0 Manual review › Browser

Googlebot smartphone render, DE storefront, via URL Inspection live testcontent present, banner not blocking Search Console › URL Inspection

Confidence is low. This is a single day manual observation on a small sample of pages, not a crawl. Googlebot appears to render the content fine, which is why I have scored the search impact low. The reason it stays in the register at all is the user experience and the accessibility exposure, and both of those are outside my measurement, so I have flagged it rather than quantified it.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Render the page content behind the banner rather than in place of it. The banner can overlay, it does not need to gate.

  1. 1Change the banner from a blocking interstitial to a bottom anchored overlay
  2. 2Keep non essential scripts gated behind consent, only the content rendering should change
  3. 3Have the accessibility reviewer confirm focus order and keyboard dismissal
  4. 4Refer the consent logic itself to counsel, it is outside the scope of this audit

Waiting on Legal sign off on any change to the consent flow

How we will know it worked

Load ten pages per EU storefront in a clean profile and confirm main content is present in the DOM and visible behind the overlay before any consent choice. Re-run the URL Inspection live test on three pages per market.

Check again by December 1, 2026.

What has happened since

Deferred by the client. Not before the Q4 legal review of the consent flow.

Client has accepted this for now. Legal review of the consent flow is scheduled for Q4 and they do not want the banner touched before that lands. Re-raise in the Q1 audit if it is still open.

Why it matters

Screaming Frog orphan URL report, cross referenced against the XML sitemap and the Shopify product export to separate live from discontinued lines.

The evidence, gathered August 11, 2026 to August 18, 2026
Product URLs in the XML sitemap with zero internal inlinks341 Screaming Frog › Orphans
Those products with organic entrances in the last 90 days12 Search Console › Performance
Products discontinued or out of stock among the 341203 Manual review › Browser

Confidence is medium. The orphan count is measured against a complete crawl and is reliable. The judgement is what to do about it, because 203 of the 341 are discontinued lines that arguably should not be in the sitemap at all. So the finding is really two, and I have kept them together because the fix is one decision.

1 Exhibit
The fix

Decide per product whether it is live or retired, then either link it or remove it from the sitemap. Leaving them orphaned but submitted is the worst of both.

  1. 1Remove the 203 discontinued products from the XML sitemap and redirect them to their closest live equivalent
  2. 2Add the 138 live products to their correct category so the normal link path picks them up
  3. 3Have platform engineering add a sitemap freshness check so retired products drop out automatically rather than being cleaned by hand

Waiting on Merchandising needs to confirm which lines are genuinely retired

How we will know it worked

Re-run the orphan report and confirm zero live products are orphaned. Fetch the XML sitemap and confirm no discontinued product URLs remain. Check that the 138 relinked products pick up impressions within eight weeks.

Check again by December 15, 2026.

What has happened since

Accepted by the client. Approved on the interim readout call.

Marked fixed on 22 August after merchandising relinked 138 products. Re-crawled on 28 August and found 47 new orphans created by the September range change, so the underlying process problem is unfixed even though the backlog was cleared. Reopened.
